chapter: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
title: Where his plunger style came from
summary: He heard plunger playing from Ellington and Joe Smith in Fletcher Henderson's band, and thinks Johnny Dunn used it.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: For instance, the way you use the plunger is pretty unique, I think. When did you start doing that?

Oh, I've been doing that for years. I used to hear bands from way back... Well, one band in particular was Duke Ellington's band. And... Well, no, Fletcher Henderson, too, had a plunger player. He had Joe Smith, who played plunger, but he played sweet horn. He was one of my idols. Just like Bobby Hackett. They seem to be the same type of guys, you know, in the way that they portrayed the solos they played. They played pretty, you know. And I liked Joe Smith very much.
And come to think of it, I think I'm... A guy named... Oh, what was his name...? Not Bubber Miley... There was a guy before Bubber Miley. What was his name?
Johnny Dunn, yeah. I think he used a lot of plunger.
